popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer's Trojan stemma names Assaracus son of Tros, brother of Ilus and Ganymede — the Dardanian branch that leads to Capys, Anchises and Aeneas.

popCulture.title: Assaracus
popCulture.description: Son of Tros, father of Capys — the quieter Dardanid king through whom Aeneas' line runs, while Ilus holds Ilium.

popCulture.title: Aeneas
popCulture.description: Assaracus' great-grandson — the Trojan who carries the Dardanian pedigree west after Troy falls.

popCulture.title: Tros
popCulture.description: Assaracus' father — eponym of Troy, whose three sons split the royal house between Ilium and Dardania.
